hypotheses.claim: H6-cvrp-regime-adaptive-rankpower-ruin: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, replacing the symmetric load-fill gate with an asymmetric edge-fill gate (penalizing both under- and over-filled routes, favoring extreme fill fractions), coupling the depot-distance gate to route extension for eccentric depots, and composing a bounded p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) schedule (0.5–4.0) will lower the mean objective below the round-5 SBS of 15.8445, with the largest per-instance gains on size=100, spatial=uniform, depot_style=eccentric, demand_dist=uniform and capacity_level=tight instances.

next_search_advice.direction: Refine the size-aware rank-power ruin hook into a regime-adaptive variant: keep the normalized multiplicative gates (removal_savings / (mean_savings * n)) but re-balance them for the currently weakest regimes reported by the archive — size=100, spatial=uniform, depot_style=eccentric, demand_dist=uniform, capacity_level=tight. Concretely (a) make the load-fill gate asymmetric: strongly favor nearly-empty and nearly-full routes under tight capacity rather than symmetric fill alone; (b) scale the depot-distance gate with route extension so eccentric depots push far-flung customers out first; (c) schedule the rank exponent p so that iter_frac drives a monotone decrease (intensification late) while stagnation_ratio drives a larger increase (diversification on stall), with the two schedules composed multiplicatively and bounded to [0.5, 4.0]; (d) shrink the top-q ruin set size proxy when n is large so more LNS iterations fit in the 500 ms clock. All additions must remain deterministic (no RNG), keep the hook read-only over input state, and preserve the 6-customer dual-action probe separation.
